description: Somos ALLPA DATA, un equipo multidisciplinario y apasionado que une talento, tecnología y el valor profundo de nuestra tierra, nuestro nombre nace del término quechua Allpa, que significa suelo o tierra, reflejando nuestra visión fundamental: «La tierra habla con datos». Combinando análisis de información, innovación tecnológica y una sólida visión estratégica, transformamos los datos satelitales en soluciones concretas para empoderar al sector agrícola.
summary: Chacra Viva (ALLPA DATA) is a decision-support tool for smallholder farmers in the Andean highlands of Cajamarca, Peru. It turns 20 years of NASA Earth observations (rainfall, surface temperature and soil moisture) into simple planting advice. A farmer locates their plot, chooses what matters most (soil health, water, frost resilience or income) and enters the crops planned for the next four seasons. The tool scores that rotation, tests all 6,561 possible four-season rotations, suggests a better one and explains why. It also shows the weekly frost risk adjusted to the farm's altitude and maps soil moisture and rain across the region. A companion mobile app reads alerts out loud and lets farmers share them by WhatsApp. Frost and tired, over-cropped soils cause heavy losses for Andean family farms; Chacra Viva gives them a free, explainable way to plan more resilient rotations, in Spanish, Quechua and English.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

Chacra Viva is a crop-rotation planner and frost-alert tool built on NASA data. It answers a practical question for Andean farmers: "What should I plant over the next four seasons, given my climate, my soil and what matters most to me?"

HOW IT WORKS (6 steps)

1. My Farm: the farmer locates the plot by GPS, a Google Maps link or a tap on the map. The tool loads NASA POWER climate data for that point, SoilGrids soil properties, and the altitude, and shows which of 9 Andean crops (potato, olluco, maize, quinoa, barley, wheat, broad bean, pea, tarwi) suit that altitude and soil.

2. Priorities: four sliders (soil health, water balance, frost resilience, estimated income) that always add up to 100%.

3. My Rotation: the farmer enters the crops planned for 4 seasons. The tool warns about repeated crops, repeated plant families and missing legumes.

4. Results: the rotation gets a 0–100 score per indicator and overall. The optimizer tests all 9^4 = 6,561 rotations, excludes unsuitable crops and consecutive repeats, suggests the best one and explains each point gained or lost.

5. Frost & Calendar: weekly frost probability from 20 years of NASA POWER surface temperature (TS_MIN), adjusted to the farmer's altitude (0.65 °C per 100 m), plus a monthly planting calendar.

6. Regional Map: soil moisture, rainfall and frost nights for 21 NASA POWER grid cells across the Cajamarca region, with NASA SMAP soil moisture and MODIS greenness layers (via NASA GIBS) for the rainy and dry seasons.

Key insight: air temperature at 2 m almost never drops below 0 °C in these valleys, but the ground surface does, and that is what burns potato and maize shoots. That is why we use surface skin temperature (TS_MIN) to estimate frost.

MOBILE APP

The Chacra Viva Flutter app brings the same data to the field: one-tap sign-in, weekly frost risk, what to do before sleeping (water at sunset, cover plants with straw), the crop to plant this year, alerts read out loud (text-to-speech), and sharing by WhatsApp with the linked phone number. It works in Spanish, Quechua and English.

BENEFITS AND IMPACT

- Free, no sign-up, works on a basic smartphone.

- Explainable: every score comes with reasons, not a black box.

- Helps reduce frost losses and soil degradation from continuous potato and maize cropping.

- Scalable: NASA POWER covers the whole planet, so the same tool can be used in any farming region by changing the data file.

TOOLS

HTML, JavaScript, Tailwind CSS, Leaflet (maps), Chart.js (charts), Python (data download and processing), Flutter/Dart (mobile app), GitHub Pages (hosting).

FACTORS WE CONSIDERED

Low connectivity and low literacy (voice, icons, WhatsApp), local languages (Quechua), altitude differences between valleys, and honesty about limits: NASA POWER cells are about 55 km wide, so the results describe the area, not the exact plot, and the scoring rules still need validation with local agronomists and SENAMHI data.

TEAM

ALLPA DATA, Cajamarca, Peru. "Allpa" means soil or land in Quechua.
